name: Pniel Ridge Sunrise
blurb: Up through the pines before first light for the moment the sun clears the Simonsberg. Coffee and rusks at the top.
description: We meet at the Pniel trailhead in the dark, headlamps on, and climb gently through a pine plantation to the ridge. As the sky lifts, you'll watch the sun break over the Simonsberg and the Winelands open up below. We'll have coffee and rusks at the summit cairn, then descend as the morning warms. A magical way to see the Boland.
imageAlt: Simonsberg and the Kylemore valley beside Pniel, seen from the Groot Drakenstein slopes

name: Botmaskop Summit
blurb: The classic Stellenbosch viewpoint — a steady climb through fynbos with the whole valley laid out behind you.
description: Starting from the Coetzenburg trails, we wind up through indigenous fynbos to the Botmaskop plateau. The climb is steady but never severe, and the payoff is the best panoramic view of Stellenbosch, the vineyards, and the mountains beyond. Perfect for those who want a proper walk with a big reward.
imageAlt: Stellenbosch Mountain rising above the Coetzenburg trails

name: Paarl Rock & the Granite Domes
blurb: Warm granite underfoot, proteas in season, and a short scramble onto the dome for lunch with a 100 km view.
description: A relaxed walk across Paarl Mountain's granite domes, perfect for families and first-timers. We follow the contour path through proteas and restios, then scramble briefly onto the second dome for lunch. The view stretches from Table Mountain to the Hex River peaks. Great for kids who like climbing on rocks.
imageAlt: The granite domes of Paarl Rock on Paarl Mountain

name: Jonkershoek Panorama Traverse
blurb: Seventeen kilometres and 1 000 m of climbing around the horseshoe. Early start, proper boots, three litres of water.
description: The big one for serious hikers. We tackle the full Jonkershoek horseshoe — up the Panorama Circuit, across the skyline, and down the waterfall route. You'll need proper boots, three litres of water, and a good head for heights. We'll reward you with the most dramatic mountain scenery in the Winelands.
imageAlt: Cloud over the Jonkershoek mountains from the hiking trail

name: Vineyard & Village Walk
blurb: A gentle loop for families — farm roads, a waterfall pool for warm days, tortoises if you look properly.
description: Our most family-friendly walk. We follow quiet farm roads between Pniel and Kylemore, past vineyards and old oak trees. There's a natural pool for a swim on warm days, and we always find tortoises and birdlife along the way. Ideal for kids and grandparents.
imageAlt: The Groot Drakenstein mountains between Pniel and Franschhoek

name: Simonsberg Full Day
blurb: The big one. Long approach, a real summit, and the Boland spread out from Table Mountain to the Hex River peaks.
description: A full-day summit attempt on Simonsberg — the iconic flat-topped mountain between Paarl and Stellenbosch. We start in the dark, take the long approach through pine and fynbos, and scramble the final pitch to the summit. On a clear day you can see from Table Mountain to the Hex River range. Not for the faint-hearted.
